options_evaluated: Fiber-reinforced composite (e.g., PA6-GF30) with TPU overmolding
assessments.recommendation: Monomaterial polymer (e.g., pure ABS) with no overmolding
assessments.rationale: Using a monomaterial polymer without overmolding ensures high ease and quality of recycling (parameter (d)) and avoids technical solutions detrimental to recycling (parameter (e), Page 79). It prevents the generation of mixed plastic waste (parameter (r), Page 80) and reduces the risk of microplastic and nanoplastic release during shredding and mechanical recycling at the end-of-life stage (parameter (p), Page 80).
assessments.potential_conflicts_with: Conflicts with the Use Phase (which may prefer TPU overmolding for ergonomic grip and impact resistance) and Manufacturing (which may prefer fiber-reinforced composites for structural strength and lightweighting).

assessments.recommendation: Threaded fasteners (screws) of a single standard type
assessments.rationale: Threaded fasteners allow non-destructive disassembly, which is essential for the ease of upgrading, reuse, remanufacturing, and refurbishment (parameter (c), Page 27, 79). This design avoids permanent bonding solutions (like adhesives or welding) that are highly detrimental to reuse and recycling (parameter (e), Page 79) and would otherwise increase the amount of waste generated (parameter (r), Page 80).
assessments.potential_conflicts_with: Conflicts with Manufacturing (who prefer ultrasonic welding or adhesives for lower assembly costs and faster production times) and Use Phase (who might prefer permanent bonding for superior dust and water ingress protection).

options_evaluated: Brushless DC motor (BLDC) with modular, clip-in mount
Brushed DC motor with integrated/soldered housing
Brushless DC motor with potted/glued electronics
assessments.recommendation: Brushless DC motor (BLDC) with modular, clip-in mount
assessments.rationale: A modular, clip-in BLDC motor facilitates easy extraction, supporting ease of upgrading, reuse, remanufacturing, and refurbishment (parameter (c), Page 27, 79). It avoids glued or potted solutions that are detrimental to recovery (parameter (e), Page 79), which would otherwise increase the consumption of energy in end-of-life treatment (parameter (g), Page 79) and generate more hazardous waste (parameter (r), Page 80).
assessments.potential_conflicts_with: Conflicts with Manufacturing (higher initial bill of materials cost for brushless technology and connectors) and Use Phase (which may favor potted electronics for extreme durability against vibration).

options_evaluated: Passive cooling via integrated aluminum heat sinks and ventilation slots
Active cooling with a glued-in fan assembly
Thermal potting compound enclosing the electronics
assessments.recommendation: Passive cooling via integrated, mechanically fastened aluminum heat sinks and ventilation slots
assessments.rationale: Passive cooling via mechanical fastening avoids the use of thermal potting compounds or adhesives, which are highly detrimental to disassembly, reuse, and recycling (parameter (e), Page 79). Potting compounds make material recovery impossible, leading to increased waste (parameter (r), Page 80) and a larger environmental footprint in end-of-life treatment (parameter (m), Page 33, 80).
assessments.potential_conflicts_with: Conflicts with Use Phase (which might require potting for dust-proofing and shock resistance in harsh environments) and Manufacturing (potting is easier to automate than mechanical heat sink assembly).

options_evaluated: Modular architecture with separate, plug-connected sub-assemblies
Partially integrated architecture with soldered wire connections
assessments.recommendation: Modular architecture with separate, plug-connected sub-assemblies
assessments.rationale: A modular, plug-connected architecture maximizes the ease of upgrading, reuse, remanufacturing, and refurbishment of individual components (parameter (c), Page 27, 79). It avoids integrated or soldered designs that are detrimental to repair and recovery (parameter (e), Page 79) and prevents the premature generation of electronic waste when only one sub-component fails (parameter (r), Page 80).
assessments.potential_conflicts_with: Conflicts with Manufacturing (due to increased assembly complexity and higher component costs for connectors and separate PCBs) and Use Phase (as modular designs can increase the overall size and weight of the tool).

options_evaluated: Removable, slide-on battery pack with standard interface and screw-fastened casing
Removable, slide-on battery pack with ultrasonically welded casing
assessments.recommendation: Removable, slide-on battery pack with standard interface and screw-fastened casing
assessments.rationale: A removable battery pack with a screw-fastened casing ensures that cells can be easily replaced, refurbished, or safely recycled (parameter (c), (d), Page 79). This avoids solutions detrimental to recovery (parameter (e), Page 79), prevents high energy consumption during end-of-life shredding/sorting (parameter (g), Page 79), and avoids the generation of hazardous waste from damaged cells (parameter (r), Page 80).
assessments.potential_conflicts_with: Conflicts with Use Phase (users may prefer a smaller, lighter integrated battery for better tool balance and ergonomics) and Manufacturing (slide-on interfaces and screw-fastened casings increase production costs).
